name: reviewer-create-change decide(approved) → coordinator wake-up
description:
ADR-057 §D5 — the create-change chain terminal. Fires when reviewer-create-change approves the drafted change. Stamps agent.run.outcome=success on the run entity (agent-run/03 completes the run) and wakes a fresh coordinator to deliver the reviewed change to the user via decide(action=respond_direct). The reviewed change IS the deliverable (renderable to OpenSpec markdown on demand); the coordinator summarises it for the user.

Mirrors research/07: same agent.run.entity_id anchor (framework-inherited across the loop-spawn chain), same outcome=success stamp, same wake-up shape restricted to respond_direct/ask_user.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
The create-change chain you dispatched has reached its terminal. Reviewer-create-change at loop $entity.instance evaluated the drafted change and approved it.

Your job now is to deliver the reviewed change to the user. You are not classifying or delegating — the chain has already done the work.

Iteration 1 — call render_openspec() to get the approved change rendered as OpenSpec markdown (proposal + requirement deltas + tasks). It reads the change off the run entity for you; omit the slug — there is exactly one change to render. Optionally call read_loop_result(loop_id=$entity.instance) for the reviewer's one-line verdict.

Iteration 2 — call decide(action="respond_direct", reason="<deliver the change to the user>"). Lead with a one-sentence summary of what the change proposes, then include the rendered OpenSpec markdown from render_openspec so the user has the actual spec, not just a description. The respond_direct rule (coordinator/03b) publishes your reason on the user-response bus.

metadata.anchor: agent.run.entity_id — framework-inherited on the reviewer (loop-spawn chain). Mirrors research/07.
metadata.render_on_demand: The wake-up coordinator calls render_openspec (ADR-057 OQ1 pair) to render the approved change.<slug>.* off the run entity to OpenSpec markdown and delivers it in respond_direct — so the user gets the actual reviewed spec, not just a prose summary. render_openspec auto-discovers the single change on the entity (no slug needed).
